_comment: RAW EVIDENCE CAPTURE — the bytes the host actually served, kept as an immutable, hash-manifested bundle. Everything else WebPivot produces is DERIVED: a favicon hash, a template fingerprint, an extracted wallet. Derived data is an assertion about a page that no longer exists — scam infrastructure is torn down in days, and once it is gone the assertion cannot be checked by anyone, including us. The capture is the primary source: the DOM as fetched, every JavaScript and stylesheet the page loaded, each with its own sha256, plus a bundle-level hash over the sorted per-file digests so any later alteration is detectable. This file holds the budgets and the classification rules that decide what a capture pulls and where it stops. Nothing here is case data.

budgets._comment: Byte and count ceilings, so one heavy SPA cannot fill a case folder and a large batch stays finishable. SAME-SITE assets are the operator's own code and get the generous budget — that is the evidence. THIRD-PARTY assets (CDN libraries, analytics, fonts) get a small one: they describe the library, not the operator, and are captured only so the manifest can state what the page loaded rather than leaving a silent hole. Anything dropped is recorded in `skipped_for_budget` on the manifest — a capture must never imply a completeness it does not have. `max_asset_bytes` caps a single file, so one 80 MB source map cannot consume the whole budget on its own.

capture_kinds._comment: Which referenced resources a capture fetches, by role. `js` and `css` are the operator's application and theme — the two that survive a re-skin and the two an analyst re-reads months later. `sourcemap` is included because a `.map` carries the developer's own directory paths and usernames. Images and fonts are NOT fetched by default: they are bulky, rarely dispositive, and the favicon (the one image that clusters) is already captured by the pivot layer as a hash. Set `fetch` true on a kind to include it.

dom.note: the served HTML, exactly as received (or as rendered, when --render is used — the manifest records which)

css.note: every stylesheet link — a shared theme is same-kit evidence and CSS is otherwise never retained

sourcemap.note: a .map beside a captured bundle: developer paths, usernames, original filenames

image.note: bulky, rarely dispositive; the favicon already clusters as a hash

manifest._comment: The evidence contract — the fields every captured file carries, and why. `sha256` is what makes the file quotable in a report; `fetched_at` (UTC) and `http_status` are what make it a dated observation rather than an undated copy; `final_url` records a redirect the analyst would otherwise never see; `content_type` is the SERVER's claim, kept even when it disagrees with the extension, because that disagreement is itself a finding. `capture_sha256` at the bundle level is computed over the sorted `sha256  relative_path` lines, so the whole capture has one citable digest and any later edit to any file changes it.

layout._comment: Where a capture lands. One directory per (host, kit, UTC timestamp) — timestamped because a re-collection of the same page later is a NEW observation, not a correction of the old one, and overwriting it would destroy the change-over-time evidence that dates a re-skin. The kit segment is in the path so a host serving several branded templates produces one directory per template rather than a single mixed pile; `_root` is used when the path carries no distinctive segment.
